note: Seed catalogue of NASA PSI combustion investigations. Every numeric test condition carries an explicit 'basis'. 'brief' = stated in the NASA PSI challenge brief. 'nominal' = representative of the investigation's published design conditions, not a per-run PSI record. 'illustrative' = placeholder used only to exercise the UI; never ranked or used as an empirical anchor. Quantitative outcomes are deliberately absent unless a basis is given, because fabricated spread rates are the one thing a fire-safety tool must never do.

investigations.name: Burning and Suppression of Solids
investigations.short: First ISS study of how solid fuels burn and are extinguished without buoyancy.

conditions.label: Artemis EVA exploration atmosphere
conditions.notes: NASA Exploration Atmosphere for Artemis/Lunar lander pre-breathe mitigation.

conditions.label: Lunar surface analog (0.166g predicted)
conditions.notes: CFD/drop-tower analog condition for PMMA rod under Moon gravity.

investigations.finding: In microgravity a quiescent solid flame tends to self-extinguish from oxygen starvation, but a very low forced flow re-supplies oxygen and sustains burning. Airflow, not buoyancy, sets the flammability limit.
investigations.partial_g_note: Defines the 0g anchor for solid fuels. Because buoyant velocity scales with sqrt(g), the forced-flow value at which spread peaks is the quantity that must be re-mapped for lunar gravity.
investigations.earth_spinoff: Cabin material screening for spacecraft and aircraft, and the airflow limits in terrestrial flammability test standards.

investigations.name: Burning and Suppression of Solids - II
investigations.short: Extended solid-fuel flammability matrix: thicker fuels, wider flow range, extinction boundaries.

conditions.label: Hypoxic cabin extinction limit
conditions.notes: Near-extinction limit under microgravity forced airflow.

conditions.label: Artemis EVA pre-breathe PMMA ignition boundary
conditions.notes: Evaluate whether reduced pressure balances oxygen enrichment for solid plastics.

investigations.finding: Spread rate is non-monotonic in airflow: it rises as flow supplies oxygen, peaks at a low characteristic velocity, then falls as convective cooling and blow-off dominate. That peak velocity is the single most gravity-sensitive parameter in the dataset.
investigations.partial_g_note: Provides the flow-response shape used to model intermediate gravity. Lunar gravity shifts the buoyant contribution but leaves the forced-flow term unchanged.
investigations.earth_spinoff: Fire-retardant textile qualification and warehouse airflow design.

investigations.name: Smoke Point In Co-flow Experiment
investigations.short: Soot formation and smoke point of gaseous co-flow diffusion flames.
investigations.finding: Microgravity co-flow flames reach a longer smoke point than 1g flames at the same fuel velocity, so soot and radiative heat transfer are under-predicted by Earth correlations.
investigations.partial_g_note: Soot yield drives radiative heat flux to nearby surfaces, which is the dominant spread mechanism in a closed habitat at elevated oxygen.
investigations.earth_spinoff: Soot-free combustor and jet engine design; diesel particulate reduction.

investigations.name: Structure and Liftoff In Combustion Experiment
investigations.short: Flame structure, stability and liftoff of gaseous jet flames in co-flow.
investigations.finding: Liftoff and blow-off limits in microgravity follow the same co-flow scaling as 1g once buoyancy is removed, which makes SLICE the cleanest dataset for isolating the forced-flow term.
investigations.partial_g_note: Because liftoff is a pure flow-structure phenomenon, it transfers to partial gravity with minimal correction - useful as a control against buoyancy-driven effects.
investigations.earth_spinoff: Burner and flare stability design, low-NOx industrial combustion.

investigations.name: Spacecraft Fire Safety Demonstration - I
investigations.short: First large-scale spacecraft fire in an uncrewed Cygnus cargo vehicle.
investigations.finding: A large-scale microgravity fire in low-pressure, elevated-oxygen air spreads at a scale where material selection dominates the outcome; the SIBAL fabric was chosen because it self-extinguishes at 1g but the test quantified how far that guarantee survives in low pressure.
investigations.partial_g_note: The only dataset at habitat-relevant size. Saffire's low pressure / high oxygen atmosphere is the closest existing analogue to the planned lunar habitat, but at 0g.
investigations.earth_spinoff: Fire limits for high-oxygen hospital, submarine and aircraft environments.

investigations.name: Spacecraft Fire Safety Demonstration - II
investigations.short: Nine material samples burned at large scale in microgravity.
investigations.finding: Material ranking in microgravity is not the same as the 1g ranking: samples that pass a 1g flammability screen can burn appreciably faster at low pressure and high oxygen.
investigations.partial_g_note: Gives a per-material ordering at 0g that can be compared against the 1g ordering - the comparison itself is a usable bound on what a lunar habitat will do.
investigations.earth_spinoff: Material qualification test methods for aerospace and rail interiors.

investigations.name: Spacecraft Fire Safety Demonstration - III
investigations.short: Largest microgravity fire to date; Saffire-III flew after the vehicle departed the ISS.
investigations.finding: Saffire-III coupled a burning sample to a downstream smoke transport path, so it measures detection latency as well as spread - the first dataset that closes the prevention-to-detection loop at scale.
investigations.partial_g_note: Detection latency depends on particle agglomeration, which is gravity-sensitive; the 0g alarm times are a lower bound on what a lunar habitat should expect.
investigations.earth_spinoff: Early-warning smoke detection in large enclosed volumes.

investigations.name: Smoke and Aerosol Measurement Experiment
investigations.short: How microgravity changes smoke particle size, and what that does to detectors.
investigations.hardware: Aerosol smoke duct with commercial detector heads
investigations.finding: Without buoyancy, smoke particles stay in the hot zone longer and agglomerate into larger particles, shifting the size distribution away from the range terrestrial detectors are tuned for.
investigations.partial_g_note: Particle residence time is set by the flow field, so detector response at 0.16g should sit between the 0g and 1g distributions rather than equal either.
investigations.earth_spinoff: Multi-criteria nuisance-free smoke detectors for homes and industry.

investigations.name: Smoke and Aerosol Measurement Experiment - Reflight
investigations.short: Reflight of SAME with improved instrumentation and more fuel types.
investigations.hardware: Aerosol smoke duct with commercial detector heads
investigations.finding: SAME-R confirmed the SAME result across more fuels and quantified how much of the size shift is due to residence time rather than fuel chemistry.
investigations.partial_g_note: Two flights of the same instrument give a repeatability estimate, which is what a detector design for a lunar habitat actually needs.
investigations.earth_spinoff: Detector calibration standards for low-airflow spaces.

investigations.name: Dust and Aerosol Measurement Feasibility Test
investigations.short: A smoke instrument repurposed to measure cabin and lunar dust.
investigations.finding: The same optical instrument that detects smoke also detects dust, which means a detector on the Moon must discriminate nuisance dust from fire signatures - a false-alarm problem created by the environment, not the sensor.
investigations.partial_g_note: Dust settling differs sharply between 0g and lunar gravity, so DAFT's 0g false-alarm rate is a pessimistic bound for a lunar habitat.
investigations.earth_spinoff: Industrial warehouse and firefighter dust/smoke sensing.

investigations.name: Dust and Aerosol Measurement Feasibility Test - 2
investigations.short: Extended dust measurement with more simulants and concentrations.
investigations.finding: DAFT-2 bounded the concentration range over which a smoke detector can be trusted in a dusty cabin, which is directly a design input for lunar surface habitats.
investigations.partial_g_note: Same instrument, wider envelope: gives the sensitivity floor a lunar detector must beat.
investigations.earth_spinoff: Nuisance-alarm reduction in mining and grain handling.

investigations.name: Flame Extinguishment Experiment
investigations.short: Liquid fuel droplet burning and extinguishment by CO2 and helium dilution.
investigations.finding: Droplet flames extinguish at a well-defined diameter in microgravity, and CO2 suppresses far more effectively than helium at the same dilution because of its heat capacity rather than its oxygen displacement.
investigations.partial_g_note: Suppression agent effectiveness is chemistry, not gravity, so FLEX's ranking of CO2 over helium transfers to lunar gravity with little correction - unlike the spread-rate data.
investigations.earth_spinoff: Fine-water-mist extinguishers, clean-agent selection, cool-flame engine concepts.

investigations.name: Flame Extinguishment Experiment - 2
investigations.short: Soot, radiative loss and near-limit droplet burning across fuels and pressures.

conditions.label: Elevated oxygen droplet combustion
conditions.notes: Investigate radiative soot loss and extinction diameter in oxygen-enriched atmosphere.

conditions.label: Martian atmospheric pressure analog
conditions.notes: Simulated low pressure droplet evaporation and burning under 0.38g.

investigations.finding: Radiative loss becomes the dominant sink near the flammability limit in microgravity, so a flame can extinguish purely by radiating heat away - a mechanism with no 1g counterpart at the same scale.
investigations.partial_g_note: Radiative extinction is scale-dependent rather than gravity-dependent, which makes FLEX-2 the most transferable dataset for lunar habitats at large sample size.
investigations.earth_spinoff: Soot models for gas turbines and fire-suppression agent sizing.

investigations.name: Cool Flames Investigation
investigations.short: Low-temperature 'cool flame' burning of droplets, invisible to the eye.
investigations.finding: Cool flames burn at temperatures far below visible ignition and can persist for many seconds, producing formaldehyde and carbon monoxide without a visible flame - a detection hazard in a crewed cabin.
investigations.partial_g_note: Cool-flame chemistry is gravity-independent; only the transport that sustains it changes. Expect the same low-temperature hazard at lunar gravity.
investigations.earth_spinoff: Low-temperature combustion engines, formaldehyde emission control.

investigations.name: ACME Cool Flames Investigation with Gases
investigations.short: Gaseous cool flames, including inside-out spherical flames at up to 85% oxygen.
investigations.finding: The highest-oxygen microgravity combustion tests in PSI: an oxygen-nitrogen mixture of up to 85% oxygen flows outward from a spherical burner into a propane-filled chamber, inverting the usual flame geometry so the oxidizer arrives from inside.
investigations.partial_g_note: This is the only PSI dataset that brackets the oxygen concentration a lunar habitat may actually use, so it anchors the high-oxygen end of any habitat risk assessment.
investigations.earth_spinoff: High-efficiency low-temperature combustion, oxygen-enriched industrial burners.

investigations.name: ACME Burning Rate Emulator
investigations.short: A gas flame that behaves like a burning solid, in still atmospheres.
fuels: gaseous simulant of a solid fuel
investigations.finding: Burning a gaseous simulant through a porous burner reproduces the heat-feedback of a solid fuel while letting material properties be varied independently - the only way to isolate which material property sets flammability in a still atmosphere.
investigations.partial_g_note: Because BRE is a still-atmosphere test, buoyancy is the only transport mechanism, so it is the most gravity-sensitive investigation in PSI and the most important to repeat at partial gravity.
investigations.earth_spinoff: Material flammability screening without destructive testing.

investigations.name: ACME Electric-Field Effects on Laminar Diffusion Flames
investigations.short: Electric fields acting on flame ions to mimic partial gravity.
investigations.finding: An applied electric field drags flame ions and induces an ion wind that reshapes the flame the way buoyancy would, so partial gravity was mimicked without ever leaving 0g.
investigations.partial_g_note: This is the closest thing to partial-gravity data in PSI, and it is still not partial-gravity data: it reproduces the flow effect of buoyancy, not the hydrostatic and heat-transfer effects.
investigations.earth_spinoff: Electrically controlled low-emission industrial burners; soot suppression.

investigations.name: ACME project (six experiments, shared hardware)
investigations.short: Advanced Combustion via Microgravity Experiments: six gaseous-fuel studies on one modular rack insert set.
investigations.hardware: ACME modular insert set (shared across all six)
investigations.finding: All six ACME experiments used the same modular hardware in the CIR, so their results are directly comparable in a way that results from different racks are not - hardware is a hidden confounder in cross-investigation comparison.
investigations.partial_g_note: Comparability across ACME runs is the template for how a lunar campaign should be designed: hold hardware fixed, vary gravity.
investigations.earth_spinoff: Modular test-rig design for industrial burner qualification.

investigations.name: ACME Coflow Laminar Diffusion Flame
investigations.short: Weak methane and ethylene co-flow diffusion flames across fuel dilution extremes (32 ISS test days).
investigations.finding: Characterized weak co-flow methane and ethylene diffusion flames across extreme nitrogen dilution levels aboard the ISS (32 test-day rows in PSI-21), anchoring computational kinetics models near extinction.
investigations.partial_g_note: Extends gaseous co-flow extinction data at 0 g; pairs with SLICE and SPICE to bound forced-flow flame stability without buoyancy.
investigations.earth_spinoff: Turbulent reacting-flow kinetic validation and low-emission industrial gas burners.

investigations.name: ACME Structure & Response of Spherical Diffusion Flames
investigations.short: Transient structure, temperature, and chemiluminescence of soot-free and sooty spherical flames.
investigations.finding: Measured transient structure and radiative response of spherical diffusion flames in both soot-free and sooty regimes aboard ISS (18 test-day records in PSI-23).
investigations.partial_g_note: Purely spherical 0 g diffusion flames set the zero-buoyancy limit for gas-phase flame spread and radiative heat loss.
investigations.earth_spinoff: Fundamental chemical kinetics validation for cleaner, higher-efficiency engine combustors.

investigations.name: Computational & Experimental Analysis of SPICE Data Sets
investigations.short: Ground/CFD re-analysis deriving temperature and soot volume fractions from 0 g SPICE vs 1 g flames.
investigations.finding: Integrated computational modeling with PSI-107 SPICE flight data to quantify why 0 g co-flow flames form more soot and higher radiative heat loads than 1 g flames.
investigations.partial_g_note: Directly bridges 0 g and 1 g soot/radiation physics, helping bound radiative preheating risk in partial-gravity habitats.
investigations.earth_spinoff: Predictive soot and radiation models for cleaner terrestrial propulsion and fire suppression.

investigations.name: Concurrent Flame Spread Modeling (FGM) vs BASS
investigations.short: Large Eddy Simulation & Flamelet Generated Manifold modeling validated against BASS tomography.
investigations.finding: Developed and validated Flamelet Generated Manifold (FGM) LES subgrid models for microgravity concurrent solid-fuel spread against BASS flight data.
investigations.partial_g_note: Provides physics-based CFD subgrid tools needed to extrapolate BASS solid flammability limits toward partial gravity.
investigations.earth_spinoff: Predictive material-flammability LES screening tools for spacecraft and terrestrial transport.

investigations.name: Advanced Smoke Modeling & Simulation from SAME Data
investigations.short: Numerical modeling quantifying how gravity drives pyrolysis smoke particle growth in SAME/SAME-R.
investigations.hardware: Aerosol smoke duct with commercial detector heads

conditions.label: pyrolysis smoke growth (0 g vs 1 g)

investigations.finding: Quantified the fluid-dynamic mechanisms separating 0 g and 1 g pyrolysis smoke particle distributions using PSI-102 SAME flight data.
investigations.partial_g_note: Links 0 g and 1 g smoke growth mechanisms so detector thresholds can be bracketed for lunar (0.16 g) and Martian (0.38 g) cabins.
investigations.earth_spinoff: Next-generation particle-aware smoke detectors for industrial and residential safety.

investigations.name: Thermo-Convective Perturbation on Cool Flame Dynamics
investigations.short: Multi-physics CFD analysis of FLEX droplet cool-flame stability and run-to-run variability.
investigations.finding: Used PSI-69 FLEX flight data to resolve how weak convective/thermal perturbations govern droplet cool-flame persistence and extinction variability.
investigations.partial_g_note: Shows how small convective velocities (such as weak lunar/Martian buoyancy) perturb near-limit cool flames.
investigations.earth_spinoff: Low-temperature engine knock mitigation and validated droplet combustion CFD models.

investigations.name: Cool Flame Transitions at Radiation / Stretch Extinction
investigations.short: Ground ozone-sensitized counterflow flames + FLEX analysis mapping cool/warm flame transitions.
investigations.finding: Revealed the double reaction-zone structure of warm diffusion flames mediating transitions between cool and hot flames across 8 summary data entries in PSI-142.
investigations.partial_g_note: Maps stretch- vs radiation-driven cool-flame limits across 1 g counterflow and 0 g FLEX data.
investigations.earth_spinoff: Ultra-lean low-temperature engine kinetics and invisible-flame hazard boundaries.

investigations.name: Cool Flame Dynamics & Thermo-Convective Perturbations (PSI-117 v2)
investigations.short: OpenFOAM 3D multi-physics CFD of n-alkane droplet cool flames under thermal and convective perturbations in microgravity.
investigations.facility: Ground Investigation / OpenFOAM CFD (NASA GRC & Univ. South Carolina)
investigations.hardware: OpenFOAM Multidimensional Multi-Physics CFD Solver + FLEX flight data

conditions.label: quiescent isolated droplet cool flame baseline
conditions.notes: 1-4 mm n-alkane droplet cool flame burning regime with radiative heat balance.

conditions.label: drift-induced convective perturbation (mimicking droplet drift)
conditions.notes: Sub-millimeter (0.5 mm) droplet subject to 2-5 cm/s unintentional drift causing oscillatory cool flame modes.

conditions.label: imposed oscillatory heat flux perturbation
conditions.notes: External thermal oscillation forcing transition between stable cool flame and warm-flame extinction.

conditions.label: ozone-assisted low-temperature chemistry boundary
conditions.notes: Ozone seeding to probe radical pool and low-temperature ignition delay boundaries.

investigations.finding: External thermo-convective perturbations shift residence time and scalar dissipation in microgravity, governing whether a cool flame self-quenches or transitions back into hot burning. Droplet drift as low as 2-5 cm/s triggers oscillatory instability.
investigations.partial_g_note: In 0g, buoyancy is suppressed, making weak convective drift and radiation the dominant transport modes. In lunar gravity (0.166g), buoyant convection overwhelms these delicate low-temperature stabilization windows.
investigations.earth_spinoff: Advances low-temperature combustion chemistry understanding relevant to internal combustion engine knock, aviation gas-turbine efficiency, and industrial CFD spray combustion modeling.
investigations.safety_implication: Identifies conditions where invisible, low-temperature cool flames can quietly smolder on fuel droplets or surfaces without triggering optical smoke detectors, and reignite if ventilation fluctuates.

upcoming.name: Lunar-g Combustion Investigation
upcoming.note: Will provide the first true partial-gravity combustion data, on the lunar surface.

upcoming.name: Flammability of Materials on the Moon
upcoming.note: Will measure material flammability at lunar gravity, closing the material-selection gap.
